newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia-backed miltia member shot in East Timor.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia-backed miltia member shot in East Timor.

text.p: Authorities are investigating the fatal shooting of the commander of one of Indonesia's miltia groups in the former Portuguese colony of East Timor, the official Antara news agency said on Saturday.

Antara quoted East Timor military commander Colonel Mahidin Simbolon as saying on Friday that Sergeant-Major Julio Fraga was shot eight times on Thursday night in Baucau, about 100 km (62 miles) east of the East Timor capital of Dili.

It said Fraga was the chief of a force of about 300 people, known as Saka, under the command of the Baquia-Baucau district military head which "protected the people" from disturbances by Fretilin, a small pro-independence guerrilla group.
Simbolon said there was an indication that a person inside the miltia had been used by Fretilin to undertake the killing. The report carried no further details of the shooting.

The Indonesian military, which officially maintains five battalions or around 3,000 troops in East Timor, has in recent years raised a number of armed local miltias as part of its strategy to localise the fight against Fretilin.
The military says fewer than 200 guerrillas remain.
Foreign military attaches believed the number of Indonesian troops in East Timor far exceeds its stated strength.

Indonesia invaded East Timor in December 1975 and unilaterally declared the territory its 27th province in July the following year. The action was not recognised by the United Nations which still regards Portugal as the administering power.
